items.longBusinessSummary: IonQ, Inc. develops quantum computing systems in the United States, Switzerland, and Internationally. It sells access to quantum computers of various qubit capacities. The company also makes access to its quantum computers through cloud platforms, such as Amazon Web Services (AWS), Braket, Microsoft's Azure Quantum, and Google's Cloud Marketplace, as well as through its cloud service. The company engages in quantum-safe communications and quantum detection systems. It provides contracts associated with the design, development, construction, and sale of specialized quantum computing hardware systems; maintenance and support services; and consulting services related to co-developing algorithms on quantum computing systems. In addition, it provides semiconductor manufacturing services. The company has a collaboration agreement with University of Chicago. The company was founded in 2015 and is headquartered in College Park, Maryland.

Title: Why IonQ Stock Fell 10% Today
Author: Anders Bylund, The Motley Fool   Mon, October 12, 2026 at 5:57 PM GMT+2 3 min read
Published: 2026-10-12T15:57:02+00:00
=== BODY ===
Quantum computing company IonQ (NYSE:IONQ) announced a $1.3 billion acquisition on Monday morning. It's an all-stock deal, and Wall Street immediately reflected the incoming dilution -- and then some. At noon ET, the stock is down 10%, lowering IonQ's total market value by $1.45 billion.
Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »
IonQ has been on a shopping spree for a while now, and privately held security expert Elisity is the latest item in the cart. This one steps outside the quantum world entirely.
Elisity makes Zero Trust security software, which runs on a simple principle: assume that nobody on the network is trustworthy, then hand out access one narrow permission at a time.
IonQ plans to combine that platform with its own post-quantum cryptography and quantum key distribution tools, then cross-sell the quantum-infused package to enterprise and government clients.
The trouble is the receipt. IonQ is paying with its own shares and didn't say how much revenue Elisity brings in. Shareholders are being asked to trust the deal without seeing any numbers, which is an odd request to make while announcing a Zero Trust acquisition.
The all-stock buyout is expected to close in the fourth quarter, pending the usual run of regulatory approvals. The actual share count will depend on IonQ's stock price, and $150 million of the total tally consists of potential earn-out bonuses based on Elisity's financial performance after closing.
Too long, didn't read? Elisity's final price may vary, and so will IonQ's resulting stock dilution.
Shareholders don't seem overly enthusiastic today. The morning's price drop removed more than the full price of the Elisity deal from IonQ's market cap. In other words, many investors think that IonQ won't benefit at all from Elisity's business.
The open questions are financial. IonQ's upcoming filings and next earnings report should shed light on Elisity's actual revenue and margins, and on whether cross-selling shows up in IonQ's multi-product revenue, which grew 40% year over year in the second quarter.

Title: IonQ Strikes up to $1.3 Billion Deal to Buy Cybersecurity Firm Elisity
Author: MT Newswires   Mon, October 12, 2026 at 6:20 PM GMT+2 2 min read
Published: 2026-10-12T16:20:27+00:00
=== BODY ===
IonQ (IONQ) has agreed to acquire cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, as the quantum computing company looks to prepare for attacks from future quantum computers.The consideration includes up to $150 million in milestone payments, IonQ said Monday. The company will issue shares at closing depending on its average share price, which must be between $33.07 and $49.61.The transaction, which requires approval from regulators, is expected to complete in the fourth quarter. IonQ's stock plunged 10% in Monday trading, taking its year-to-date loss to 20%. IonQ said the combined platform will protect against current large language model and emerging quantum threats."Q-Day is coming much faster than predicted," IonQ Chief Executive Niccolo de Masi said in the statement, referring to a point when quantum computers become powerful enough to break public-key encryption used to secure digital communications, identities and transactions."Elisity will bring proven enterprise policy enforcement scale and deployment experience to our quantum security strategy and will give IonQ a strong growth platform to serve customers and create value for our shareholders," de Masi said.Elisity will continue operating under its current leadership, including CEO James Winebrenner, IonQ said. "With IonQ, we will be optimally positioned to partner with them to modernize their crypto-agility programs, accelerate post-quantum cryptography capabilities while advancing their holistic Zero Trust posture and deploy hybrid-cybersecurity solutions today that are prepared for the quantum future," Winebrenner said in the statement.Wedbush Securities described the deal as a "sensible channel play" for IonQ that extends its security assets amid a recent flurry of cybersecurity merger and acquisition activity. The all-stock structure makes sense given IonQ's cash needs, but an estimated $1.15 billion in upfront consideration implies about 23 million to 35 million new shares, adding to dilution concerns, analyst Matt Bryson wrote in a note.Last month, IonQ said it expects its full-year 2026 revenue of $450 million to $460 million, reflecting contributions from chipmaker SkyWater Technology, which it acquired at the end of July. The consensus on FactSet is for $445.3 million. Last year, the company completed the purchase of UK-based quantum computing company Oxford Ionics in a deal worth $1.08 billion.In the broader industry, consulting firm Accenture (ACN) announced three acquisition deals in June worth about $4.18 billion to expand its cybersecurity capabilities. In March, Alphabet's (GOOG, GOOGL) Google completed its $32 billion acquisition of cloud security platform Wiz. Earlier in the year, Palo Alto Networks (PANW) closed its $25 billion acquisition of identity security vendor CyberArk. Last month, Palo Alto CEO Nikesh Arora said the company expects AI tailwinds driving cybersecurity demand to intensify in the future. In late August, CrowdStrike (CRWD) raised its full-year net new annual recurring revenue outlook amid increasing demand for cybersecurity solutions to address AI risks.

Title: Top Midday Stories: Starbucks Says It's Not Buying Chipotle; IonQ Buying Elisity for Up to $1.3 Billion
Author: MT Newswires   Mon, October 12, 2026 at 5:48 PM GMT+2 1 min read
Published: 2026-10-12T15:48:37+00:00
=== BODY ===
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up in late-morning trading Monday, while the S&P 500 Index and Nasdaq Composite were down, as investors look ahead to critical earnings results and inflation data releases. In company news, Starbucks (SBUX) told MT Newswires it is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG), refuting reporting from last week. Starbucks shares were up 1.3% around midday, while Chipotle shares were down 4.6%. IonQ (IONQ) said Monday it signed an agreement to acquire cybersecurity firm Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion. The deal will include up to $150 million in earnout opportunity, depending on Elisity's performance, the company said. IonQ shares were down 9.5%. Microsoft (MSFT) said Monday it is scaling its Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments, beginning in 2027, which will make Maia the primary inference system for Microsoft products and services. Microsoft shares were up 1.2%. Nvidia (NVDA) is in talks to acquire open model startup Reflection AI, the Financial Times reported Saturday, citing people with direct knowledge of the matter. Nvidia shares were down 1.6%. Amazon (AMZN) is in talks to acquire AI startup Decart in a $7 billion deal, The Wall Street Journal reported Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. Amazon shares were down 0.4%. Salesforce (CRM) has entered a definitive agreement to acquire Loops, an AI-powered analytics platform, the company said Monday. The deal is expected to close in early November of Salesforce's fiscal 2027, the company said. Financial terms were not disclosed. Salesforce shares were up 2.1%. Delta Air Lines (DAL) said Monday it is delaying the planned launch of nonstop flights between Atlanta and Riyadh, Saudi Arabia until March 2027 due to safety and security concerns. Delta shares were down 1.4%.
